description: Observed or officially estimated visitation for San Francisco parks, for calibrating the beta3 park attraction term. Every number below was read from the fetched source cited with it; raw downloads (and text extractions of PDFs) are in data/beta3/raw/parks-visits/ (gitignored). Nothing here is extrapolated or modelled by us. Where a value is a vehicle count, a cumulative total, or a partial-area screenline count, it is labelled as such and annualVisits is null.

parks.name: Golden Gate Park
parks.year: not stated (undated agency web page, current at access)
parks.method: Official round-number estimate ('an estimated 24 million visitors each year'). The page gives no methodology, counting period or definition of a visit. RPD's FY23 annual report (below) says RPD measures JFK Promenade use with hand counts, passive infrared sensors and location-based (cell phone) data, but it does not tie the 24 million figure to any of these.

source.publisher: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department
source.title: Getting to Golden Gate Park
source.page: intro paragraph: 'We're proud to welcome an estimated 24 million visitors each year to Golden Gate Park'; same section gives '1,017-acre, three-mile-long urban park'

parks.name: Golden Gate Park - car-free JFK Drive (JFK Promenade) trips
parks.period: late April 2020 to about September 2021 (about 17 months)
parks.method: Counts of people walking, rolling, biking on car-free JFK Drive ('almost 7 million ... trips'); stated as 36% more daily park trips on JFK than before the closure. Counting technology not stated in the deck; RPD's FY23 annual report (p.4) says JFK visitation is measured with hand counts, passive infrared sensors (which cannot distinguish mode) and location-based data. Covers the JFK corridor only, not the whole park.

source.publisher: SFMTA and SF Recreation and Park Department
source.title: Golden Gate Park Access & Safety Program (presentation)
source.page: slide 8 ('Almost 7 million walking, rolling, biking and strolling trips have been made on car-free JFK since April 2020, a 36% daily increase in park visits'); repeated on the program fact sheet https://sfrecpark.org/DocumentCenter/View/17286/GGP-Access-Fact-Sheet p.1

parks.name: Golden Gate Park (eastern end, JFK Drive area) - Saturday vs Sunday screenline counts
parks.method: Manual screenline counts of all pedestrians, cyclists, roller skaters and skateboarders passing 5 points on or near JFK Drive, 1-3pm only, on 2 Saturdays and 2 Sundays (Aug 5-6 sunny, Aug 19-20 foggy, 2006), plus a 763-response intercept survey. JFK was closed to cars on Sundays. Counts are summed across the two days of each type ('combined Saturdays' vs 'combined Sundays').
parks.otherFindings: Intercept survey: 31% walked to the park; about 31% reached it in under 10 minutes; fewer than 10% travelled an hour or more; 11% took transit (p.5-6). The study notes the survey covers only the JFK area and 'can not be extrapolated to uses of all areas within Golden Gate Park'.

source.title: Golden Gate Park Transportation Access Summer 2006: Weekend Access Conditions
source.page: pp.1-3 of 8 (PDF pp.3-5), 'Methodology' and 'Pedestrian & Bicycle Access'

parks.name: Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GOGA), whole unit
parks.method: NPS official recreation visits (sum of the 12 monthly values from the IRMA visitation service). Built from the GOGA counting instructions (Jan 2023): Alcatraz concessioner ticket counts; inductive-loop vehicle counters at each site multiplied by persons-per-vehicle (1.7 to 2.8) after subtracting non-reportable vehicles; Crissy Field trail counters (Mason St path, Promenade) divided by 2; special-event counts; Ocean Beach walk-in regression; Cliff House restaurant patrons. Includes Marin and San Mateo sites and Alcatraz. Does NOT include Muir Woods NM, Fort Point NHS or SF Maritime NHP (separate NPS units). Presidio Trust-managed lands are not counted by these instructions apart from the NPS-run Crissy Field, Fort Scott overlook and Baker Beach counters.

siteVehicleCounts.description: NPS inductive-loop VEHICLE counts (not people) at GGNRA sites in San Francisco, annual totals from the IRMA 'Traffic Counts' park report. To turn them into NPS recreation visits, NPS subtracts a fixed number of non-reportable vehicles and multiplies by persons-per-vehicle (PPV), as listed here from the Jan 2023 counting instructions. We have NOT applied these factors. Many months are clearly filled or estimated (identical values repeat, e.g. Ocean Beach Second Overlook 12,477 every month 2019-2024; Sloat 28,781 every month 2022-2024), so treat the Ocean Beach series especially as NPS estimates, not fresh counts. Monthly values are in the raw file.

source.publisher: U.S. National Park Service (IRMA Visitor Use Statistics)
source.title: Park Specific Reports: Traffic Counts (Golden Gate NRA)
source.page: per-location tables

benchmarks.name: U.S. neighborhood parks, observed use (SOPARC direct observation)
benchmarks.value: Average neighborhood park of 8.8 acres averaged 20 users/hour, or an estimated 1,533 person-hours of weekly use

notes: Golden Gate Park's 24 million/yr is an undated round-number RPD claim with no published method. The only published GGP counts are the JFK Promenade sensor/LBD series (charted, not tabulated, in RPD's FY23 annual report p.4-5) and the 2006 SFCTA weekend screenlines. Museum and garden attendance at the Concourse in FY23 was about 3.46M (Cal Academy 1.18M + de Young 1.07M + three gardens 1.21M), i.e. the attraction-only share of the 24M claim.
The FY23 RPD annual report has a monthly 'Concourse Garage Transient Revenue' table (dollars, not visits). We did not record it as visitation.
No later (FY24/FY25) Golden Gate Park Access and Safety annual report was found on sfrecpark.org; the JFK Access page lists only the FY23 annual report and 2022-2023 quarterlies.

Presidio (9.5M, 2024) and GGNRA (15.7M, 2025) are counted by different agencies and methods (cellphone data plus trail counters vs vehicle counters times PPV). Crissy Field, Baker Beach and Fort Scott overlook are NPS-counted sites inside the Presidio and are probably also in the Trust's cellphone-based total. Neither source says how they overlap, so do not add the two totals together for the Presidio area.

GOGA's 15.7M covers sites in Marin and San Mateo counties too (Marin Headlands, Fort Baker, Stinson, Muir Beach, Tennessee Valley, Bolinas Ridge, etc.) plus Alcatraz. NPS does not publish a per-site person count; per-site vehicle counts and the PPV multipliers are under siteVehicleCounts.

The IRMA SSRS 'GOGA YTD Report' (which may hold per-field visitor numbers) returned 'Service unavailable' twice on 2026-10-04. The 'Monthly Public Use' report gives only unit totals. The Crissy Field trail-counter and Alcatraz concessioner monthly values were therefore not obtained.

Not found or not fetchable: NRPA does not publish a visits-per-acre benchmark (Park Metrics covers budgets, staffing, acreage per resident). We found no visitation counts for McLaren Park, Lake Merced, Twin Peaks or other RPD parks from RPD, the Controller, SFCTA or SF Planning. Trust for Public Land ParkScore rates access and acreage, not visits. We found no Placer.ai or mobile-data park estimates published by an official SF body (StreetLight's GGP case study page gives no numbers). Lands End: secondary pages cite '1 million visitors each year' and an NPS 48-hour survey of 'nearly 5,800 people', but the American Trails page that carries them returned HTTP 403 and the Parks Conservancy Lands End pages fetched do not contain them, so they are not recorded. Dolores Park: only a 2016 Chronicle figure, recorded with low confidence.

Day-type splits available: Presidio quarterly (2018-2020); GOGA, FOPO, SAFR, MUWO monthly; Cal Academy monthly (FY18-FY23); 2006 GGP Saturday vs Sunday screenlines (JFK closed Sundays); Dolores Park weekend vs weekday (press). None of the official sources gives a weekday/weekend split for annual visits.
